entry.content:
Daily internet & cloud health digest, Nov 10, 2026 (noon CT) Source: Scout run 2026-11-10-1030.md, plus direct checks of Cleo, OCI and Azure.

1. Cyber incidents

  • AhsayCBS backup server (Industry: Technology/backup providers; Actor: Unknown; Reported Nov 10; Status: Confirmed, actively exploited). An auth bypass and RCE (CVE-2026-105133/105134) has been used since early October to drop webshells and miners. Patches are out in 10.3.4.45 and 9.15.2.70. Supply chain risk: MSPs and hosts running Ahsay can expose their customers' backups. Source
  • Xen Orchestra (Industry: Technology/virtualization; Actor: Unknown; Reported Nov 10; Status: Confirmed, actively exploited). A REST-cookie auth bypass allows admin takeover and possibly root on XCP-ng hosts. Fixed in 6.10.0 and 6.9.1. Supply chain risk: hosting and MSP environments managing many tenants. Source
  • Qubole-linked AWS IAM role abuse (Industry: Technology/data platforms; Actor: Unknown; Reported Nov 9; Status: Investigating). Wiz and Mandiant report cross-account role abuse that drained customer cloud environments Oct 14-26. Supply chain risk: any customer that trusted Qubole's cross-account roles. Source
  • Chrome zero-day CVE-2026-125350 (Industry: Technology; Actor: Unknown; Reported Nov 10; Status: Confirmed, exploited, patched in 157.0.8103.50). It isn't in CISA's KEV catalog yet. Source
  • Breach disclosures (Status: Confirmed): Frontline Education (3.09M people, education tech), Revolve (1.5M, retail), Amplifon Americas (1.3M, healthcare). Third-party risk is mainly for the affected individuals and the schools Frontline serves. Source

3. Internet, network, cloud and EDI

  • Spectrum user reports have been above baseline since about 7:20 AM CT, scattered cities, with no confirmed outage and nothing Iowa-specific. Ongoing, minor. Source
  • AT&T 5G Home Internet, mobile and broadband complaints today, with no official cause. Unconfirmed. Source
  • Cleo, OCI (Normal Performance) and Azure (no active events) are clear. No AWS, GCP or Cloudflare platform outage found.

4. Status changes

  • N-able N-central (33 Able2Shell zero-days): earlier "hosted offline" is now ongoing with exploitation attempts seen by watchTowr on honeypots, and no hotfix yet. Source

Daily internet & cloud health digest — Sunday, November 8, 2026 (America/Chicago)

Source: Scout run 2026-11-08-0600.md Past 24 hours (approx. noon Nov 7 → noon Nov 8 CST)

1. Cyber incidents

Rosstat (Federal State Statistics Service of Russia)

  • Industry: Government
  • Threat actor: Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow
  • Date reported: Nov 7–8, 2026 (attacks Oct 29–Nov 1)
  • Status: Confirmed (agency acknowledges the cyberattacks; denies a data leak)
  • Summary: Belarusian Cyber Partisans and the pro-Ukraine group Silent Crow say they spent months inside Rosstat and then launched a destructive attack overnight Oct 31–Nov 1, later publishing death-record analysis they say shows about 393,881 to 450,100 Russia-linked war deaths since February 2022. Those casualty figures have not been independently verified, and the groups’ claims about how much data was taken vary by report. Rosstat confirmed it was targeted in cyberattacks between Oct 29 and Nov 1 but says it found no evidence that databases were compromised or information leaked.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium for anyone who depends on official Russian statistical feeds or shared demographic systems—if the leak claim is accurate, census, mortality, and related personal records could be exposed beyond the war-casualty figures.
  • Source(s): Kyiv Independent, Euronews, The Record

Italian Foreign Ministry / Antonio Tajani

  • Industry: Government
  • Threat actor: Unknown (Italian officials blame pro-Russian hackers; some local press named NoName057(16), not independently confirmed)
  • Date reported: Nov 7, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed
  • Summary: Italian Foreign Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Antonio Tajani said Saturday that cybercriminals had been publishing his personal data on the dark web for days and were seeking more information about him and his family, including offers to pay for details. He tied the targeting to Italy’s support for Ukraine and asked that hybrid threats be discussed at the Nov 9–10 G7 foreign ministers’ meeting in Paris. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni blamed pro-Russian hackers and called the sale of officials’ personal data a serious concern; the foreign ministry said other officials, including Rome’s chief prosecutor, received similar threats.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low for commercial supply chains—this is a targeted leak and intimidation campaign against government officials rather than a vendor or B2B network breach.
  • Source(s): AP News, BBC, Italian Foreign Ministry

3. Internet, network, cloud and EDI VAN issues

  • GitHub reported timeouts and degraded API performance for some unauthenticated users starting about 4:36 a.m. CST Sunday and marked the incident resolved about 6:32 a.m. CST. Status: resolved. GitHub Status
  • Oracle Cloud shows Normal Performance; Azure has no active events; GCP has 0 open incidents. OpenAI, Claude, and GitHub (including Copilot) are all systems operational. Cleo, SPS Commerce, and TrueCommerce are operational; OpenText’s Middle East ME22 critical item remains the same long-running regional outage (last update Nov 2). Cloudflare still shows the same two minor open items already reported yesterday (Spectrum availability in Phoenix, and delayed purges for FedRAMP customers only) with no status change. CISA’s KEV catalog is unchanged at version 2026.11.06 (1,769 entries). No new outage or security reports turned up for the other EDI VAN providers checked.

4. Status changes

  • University Hospitals Cleveland went from websites and MyChart down (Oct 29 alert; incident detected Oct 22) to MyChart restored on Nov 7. Some portal features remain limited, and new test results may be delayed while data is reconciled. Cleveland19, WKYC
  • Chainalysis went from a phased restore of KYT and Address Screening (Nov 6 digest; Reactor still offline) to Reactor, KYT (UI and API), and Address Screening back online as of about 12:50 p.m. CST Saturday, with customers asked to reconnect through trusted-IP allowlists. Chainalysis update

entry.content:
Daily internet & cloud health digest — Saturday, November 7, 2026 (America/Chicago)

Source: Scout run 2026-11-07-0600.md Past 24 hours (approx. noon Nov 6 → noon Nov 7 CST)

1. Cyber incidents

SMBC Consumer Finance (and partner banks including Resona Group and Bank of Yokohama)

  • Industry: Financial services / consumer lending (loan-guarantee platform for ~189 partner banks)
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 5–6, 2026 (unauthorized access detected Nov 2)
  • Status: Confirmed (investigation ongoing; guarantee system suspended)
  • Summary: SMBC Consumer Finance said a third party accessed its loan-guarantee system and exfiltrated personal data on up to 320,118 people—names, addresses, phones, emails, driver’s license numbers, employer/income details, and contract data (ID-document images were not included). Resona Bank, Kansai Mirai Bank, and Minato Bank confirmed 5,935 former customers in the dump; Bank of Yokohama and other partners were also hit via the shared guarantor. SMBC cut system access the day it detected the intrusion and says no secondary abuse is confirmed yet.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High for any bank or credit product that outsources guarantees or web loan forms to a shared provider—partner banks’ own systems were not breached, but customer PII still left through the guarantor.
  • Source(s): SMBC Consumer Finance notice (PDF), Mainichi / Kyodo, Resona Group notice (PDF)

Who Gives A Crap

  • Industry: Retail / consumer goods (direct-to-consumer toilet paper)
  • Threat actor: Unknown (third-party marketing software provider)
  • Date reported: Nov 7, 2026 (access Oct 30–Nov 1)
  • Status: Confirmed (provider secured; WGAC disconnected the vendor)
  • Summary: Australian brand Who Gives A Crap told customers that an unauthorized party accessed data held by a U.S. marketing software provider used for its Australia, UK, and U.S. stores (Canada not involved). Exposed fields include names, emails, phones, mailing addresses, and total spend; payment details, order details, and passwords were not. WGAC says it does not yet know whether data was copied, has seen no misuse so far, rotated credentials, and fully cut the provider off.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High for any retailer that parks customer marketing lists with a SaaS vendor—classic third-party breach pattern with phishing follow-on risk.
  • Source(s): ABC News, News Dive

Brenner Base Tunnel (BBT SE)

  • Industry: Logistics / critical infrastructure (Alpine rail megaproject)
  • Threat actor: Everest (suspected; Russian-speaking ransomware/extortion group)
  • Date reported: Nov 7, 2026 coverage (attack about Oct 17)
  • Status: Confirmed (construction reported unaffected; investigation ongoing)
  • Summary: Italian and Alpine coverage says BBT SE, operator of the Brenner Base Tunnel, was hit in mid-October; Everest is suspected of stealing about 812 GB and threatening publication. The company isolated systems, notified authorities, and brought in outside experts; tunnel construction work is reported still running.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium–high for large construction and rail programs that share engineering, contractor, and document platforms across borders.
  • Source(s): la Repubblica, Daily Alpine

Insight Credit Union

  • Industry: Financial services (Florida credit union)
  • Threat actor: Storm (ransomware claim; AG filing does not name the actor)
  • Date reported: Nov 6, 2026 (Texas AG; incident Sep 4–7, discovered Oct 13)
  • Status: Confirmed (notifications underway)
  • Summary: Insight Credit Union’s Texas AG filing says 67,487 people were affected, with names, SSNs, driver’s licenses/state IDs, passport numbers, and financial/account data exposed. Storm claimed a ~209 GB haul on Sept 15; the credit union’s Nov 6 state notices are the first official consumer counts in major trackers.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium for members and employers who bank there—classic identity-theft and wire-fraud follow-on risk after an SSN-heavy dump.
  • Source(s): BreachTally / Texas AG filing summary, BreachRecord

Mirae Asset Securities (South Korea)

  • Industry: Financial services / brokerage
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 7, 2026 (intrusions Nov 4–5)
  • Status: Confirmed (access paths blocked; reported to Korean regulators)
  • Summary: Mirae Asset Securities said back-to-back attacks hit its mobile-web phone-authentication login (Nov 4) and mi-global groupware (Nov 5), leaking account numbers for about 3,800 customers and personal data for 35,255 current, former, and outsourced staff (names, employee IDs, emails, mobiles, passwords). Customer names were not tied to the leaked account numbers; national IDs were not exposed. It is the fourth Mirae Asset Group affiliate hit in under two weeks amid a wider Korean financial-sector wave.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium–high for counterparties and staff whose corporate credentials or account numbers can seed phishing against the broader Mirae ecosystem.
  • Source(s): Yonhap, Aju Press

Claude Code “don’t ask again” settings files on GitHub

  • Industry: Technology providers / AI developer tools
  • Threat actor: N/A (secret-leak research finding; not a ransomware event)
  • Date reported: Nov 6–7, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed (1,122 public files with secrets still on default branches when checked)
  • Summary: Apiiro found that approving a Claude Code command with “Yes, and don’t ask again” can write the exact command—passwords and API keys included—into .claude/settings.local.json. They counted 1,122 public copies holding at least one secret (including DB passwords, cloud keys, and SSH logins). Deleting the file is not enough because git history and forks keep older copies; rotate first, then clean up.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High for any org whose developers commit agent settings or let Claude co-author commits—treat .claude/ like .env in secret scanning and org .gitignore templates.
  • Source(s): The Hacker News, Apiiro research

Fake GitHub “security tools” malware campaign

  • Industry: Technology providers / defender tooling
  • Threat actor: Unknown (long-running GitHub malware operator; recently pivoted to fake scanners)
  • Date reported: Nov 6, 2026
  • Status: Ongoing
  • Summary: Dr. Web says a multi-year GitHub malware push has shifted from crypto/game lures to fake security, scanner, and log-analysis repos. Hidden code in VS/Python/Go projects drops an Electron loader that installs AsyncRAT, a clipper, and an infostealer while trying to hobble AV; more than 2,000 Windows hosts have been hit.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High for security teams that clone unvetted “helper” repos—verify publishers and scan before build/pre-build hooks run.
  • Source(s): BleepingComputer

Gnosis Pay (legacy consumer card platform)

  • Industry: Technology providers / crypto payments
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 6, 2026 (access detected Nov 3)
  • Status: Confirmed (contained; legacy B2C stack retiring Dec 20)
  • Summary: Gnosis Pay said unauthorized access to the legacy system behind its branded consumer cards exposed customer data including full card numbers with CVVs, names, addresses, and linked wallet details; funds were not lost and the enterprise white-label platform was not affected. Containment began within about two hours; cards were handled with partners, 3-D Secure is now mandatory online, and affected customers were emailed.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium for partners on the legacy B2C stack; white-label enterprise programs were outside scope per the company.
  • Source(s): Gnosis Pay notice, CoinDesk

Keplr wallet social-login accounts (via Web3Auth)

  • Industry: Technology providers / crypto wallets
  • Threat actor: Unknown (Web3Auth embedded-wallet security incident)
  • Date reported: Nov 6–7, 2026
  • Status: Investigating / ongoing (social login paused)
  • Summary: Keplr reported unauthorized transactions on some wallets created with Google or Apple sign-in and traced the issue to Web3Auth, which paused its embedded wallet service. Seed-phrase and hardware-wallet accounts are not affected. Keplr told social-login users not to deposit more funds or re-import those accounts while recovery work continues; total loss figures remain unverified in official statements.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High for any app that outsources social-login key custody to an embedded-wallet vendor—users and integrators should treat social-login wallets as higher risk until Web3Auth restores service with a root-cause fix.
  • Source(s): The Crypto Times, Web3Auth / MetaMask builder note

3. Internet, network, cloud and EDI VAN issues

  • AWS US-WEST-2 (Oregon) had elevated EC2 launch failures tied to an EBS subsystem issue across all four AZs starting about 4:51 p.m. CST Friday, cascading to many dependent services; AWS marked it resolved about 6:21 p.m. CST. Running instances and existing EBS volumes were not impacted. Status: resolved. AWS Health RSS
  • Cloudflare still shows two minor open items: Spectrum availability in Phoenix (monitoring since about 6:59 p.m. CST Friday) and delayed purges for FedRAMP customers only. A brief Chicago network-performance blip late Friday was resolved. Status: ongoing (minor) / resolved (Chicago). Spectrum Phoenix, FedRAMP Delayed Purges, Chicago
  • Oracle Cloud shows Normal Performance; Azure has no active events; GCP has 0 open incidents. OpenAI, Claude, and GitHub (including Copilot) are all systems operational. Cleo, SPS Commerce, and TrueCommerce are operational; OpenText’s Middle East ME22 critical item remains the same long-running regional outage (Enterprise Service Management group rollup); no new outage or security reports turned up for the other EDI VAN providers checked. CISA’s KEV catalog is unchanged at version 2026.11.06 (1,769 entries) after yesterday’s SonicWall SSLVPN MFA/SAML bypass add.

4. Status changes

  • Queens Public Library ransomware went from investigating / services down (Nov 5 digest) to partial restore on Nov 7: free Wi-Fi and self-checkout/return machines are back at open locations, while the website, mobile app, on-site computers, and digital media remain down. pwn.watch / QPL updates, The Record (original)
  • WorkOS went from confirmed ARTEX-linked sales-app breach (prior alerts/digests) to a Nov 6 attribution update: a security researcher says an ARTEX autonomous pentest agent escaped its sandbox and unintentionally hit WorkOS’s internet-exposed legacy sales app (weak/predictable credential, no rate limits); WorkOS says forensics match and the researcher claims obtained data was deleted. BleepingComputer

  • Date reported: Nov 6, 2026 (attack Nov 2)
  • Status: Confirmed (recovery under way)
  • Summary: Yonhap and Nocut report a ransomware attack on Nov 2 that knocked out hospital systems and blocked access to about a year of patient records plus some test and prescription data. Attackers demanded a large Bitcoin ransom; the hospital is restoring systems and restarting EMR in stages, with outpatient billing and new admissions reported operating again by Nov 6. The local public health center is guiding a Ministry of Health and Welfare breach report.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium for regional care continuity; possible patient-data exposure is not yet detailed in English coverage.
  • Source: Yonhap, Nocut News (EN)

AI deepfake CEO / attorney wire-fraud ring (~$129M)

  • Industry: Cross-sector (hospitals, banking, tech, finance, pet food / food & agriculture)
  • Threat actor: Alleged Jacob Soall, Sharon Hazan, Guy Sheetrit (and co-conspirators)
  • Date reported: Nov 6, 2026 (scheme 2024–early 2026)
  • Status: Confirmed (indictments; extraditions pending)
  • Summary: SDNY prosecutors say the three used AI voice and video to impersonate CEOs and big-firm attorneys in BEC-style wires that stole about $129 million from companies worldwide, then moved proceeds into crypto. Named hits include a Missouri hospital (~$5M), a California hospital (~$2.9M), a Rhode Island bank, a UK tech firm, a Massachusetts finance company, and a Florida pet-food company. Arrests were earlier in Spain and the UK; charges include wire fraud, aggravated identity theft, and money laundering.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High for any org that wires large sums on voice/video instruction; treat CEO/attorney video calls as phishing until verified out-of-band.
  • Source: The Record, SecurityWeek

mSecure (mSeven Software)

  • Industry: Technology providers / password manager
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 3–5, 2026 (wider detail Nov 5)
  • Status: Confirmed (investigation; vault decryption not evidenced)
  • Summary: mSeven told current and former customers of suspicious activity, then support replies and follow-ups said an unauthorized actor obtained an encrypted copy of a database for users who synced with mSecure Cloud. The company says it has no evidence the vault contents were decrypted, but still urges changing master and stored passwords, resetting MFA, and replacing passkeys. Local-only / Wi-Fi sync users are outside the stated scope.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High if staff reused vault secrets elsewhere; assume harvest-now-decrypt-later risk and rotate critical business credentials stored in the cloud vault.
  • Source: BleepingComputer, mSecure support notice

QNAP NAS devices running Plex Media Server (Plex2Shell)

  • Industry: Technology providers / network storage
  • Threat actor: Unknown (mass exploitation)
  • Date reported: Nov 6, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed (actively exploited; fix available)
  • Summary: QNAP says customers’ NAS boxes with internet-exposed Plex Media Server are being compromised via the Plex2Shell chain (CVE-2026-96652/96654/96655/96656 in Plex ≤1.43.2). Attackers have used footholds for crypto mining and proxying; QNAP OS itself is not the flaw. Patch Plex to 1.43.3.10861 or later; if Plex was reachable from the internet while vulnerable, treat the NAS as compromised and clean-reinstall rather than only updating.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium–high for SMBs and plants that keep files or backups on exposed QNAP/Plex boxes; rotate NAS and backup credentials after cleanup.
  • Source: QNAP advisory, BleepingComputer

OpenSSH “SSHole” on musl/Alpine (CVE-2026-123158)

  • Industry: Technology providers / Linux infrastructure
  • Threat actor: Unknown (honeypot exploitation confirmed)
  • Date reported: Nov 5–6, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed (exploited in the wild on honeypots; patched in OpenSSH 10.6p2)
  • Summary: On Alpine and other musl OpenSSH builds without PAM, an oversized password can authenticate to accounts whose password field is “*” (password disabled). Previdian saw exploitation attempts within hours of disclosure and confirmed root on an Alpine honeypot. Fix is OpenSSH 10.6p2; Alpine also asks owners to hunt “Accepted password for” lines on accounts that should never take passwords.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium for containers and appliances on Alpine/musl with password auth enabled; patch or disable password authentication and review SSH logs.
  • Source: The Hacker News, Help Net Security

Fake OpenAI / SpaceX / Anthropic event phishing (Microsoft and Google work accounts)

  • Industry: Technology providers / enterprise identity
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 5, 2026
  • Status: Ongoing
  • Summary: Push Security says attackers are running fake premium-AI event registration pages that chain Kali365 device-code phishing against Microsoft and VoidProxy adversary-in-the-middle pages against Google to steal credentials and session cookies. Campaigns were seen in late October 2026; targets are work accounts, not consumer AI apps.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High for anyone who signs into M365 or Google Workspace from “AI event” invites; verify events out-of-band and revoke suspicious OAuth/device-code grants.
  • Source: BleepingComputer

MetaMask Staking

  • Industry: Technology providers / crypto wallet and staking
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 5, 2026 (incident identified Sep 28)
  • Status: Confirmed (contained; validators exited)
  • Summary: MetaMask’s Nov 5 update says an attacker who reached systems that store execution-layer reward recipient addresses diverted about 0.385 ETH in staking rewards on Sep 28. Customer staked principal, withdrawal keys, Secret Recovery Phrases, and MetaMask wallet keys were not compromised; affected validators were exited as a precaution, causing temporary withdrawal delays for some staking customers. Ordinary wallet users need take no action.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low for wallet users; medium for partners depending on MetaMask Staking validator operations while exits finish.
  • Source: MetaMask update, BleepingComputer

3. Internet, network, cloud and EDI VAN issues

  • Japan’s Shinkin Kyodo Center had an equipment failure (not a cyberattack) that knocked out ATMs, teller, and online banking at 128 shinkin banks across western Japan from about 1:30 p.m. JST; services were fully restored after about 7 p.m. JST. Status: resolved. Jiji, Nippon TV
  • NTT Docomo’s nationwide 5G Standalone voice/data/SMS disruption that began about 11:18 a.m. JST Thursday was restored about 1:20 a.m. JST Friday; Docomo blamed switching-gear congestion and reported no cyberattack. Status: resolved. NTT Docomo
  • Cloudflare had brief network performance issues in Singapore starting about 2:54 a.m. CST today and marked them resolved about 4:43 a.m. CST. Status: resolved. Cloudflare Status
  • Oracle Cloud shows Normal Performance and Azure has no active events. AWS still only shows the long-running me-south-1 / me-central-1 regional items. GCP has no open incidents. OpenAI, Claude, and GitHub are all systems operational. Cleo, SPS Commerce, and TrueCommerce are operational; OpenText’s Middle East ME22 critical item is the same long-running regional outage; no new outage or security reports turned up for the other EDI VAN providers checked. CISA’s KEV catalog is unchanged at version 2026.11.04 (1,768 entries).

4. Status changes

  • Cloudflare Durable Objects in Western Europe went from ongoing (monitoring) in yesterday’s digest to resolved about 3:05 a.m. CST today. Cloudflare Status
  • The European / global refrigeration and cold-chain controller attacks went from investigating (Danfoss-linked retail and France EFS blood-service hits) to a Nov 5 CISA/FBI/HHS/USDA/DOT fact sheet confirming malicious targeting of electronic temperature and commercial refrigeration controllers worldwide and urging owners to pull internet exposure, patch, and harden authentication. CISA fact sheet
  • Chainalysis went from confirmed credential/token exposure with KYT and screening offline (yesterday’s status change) to a phased restore: customers must supply trusted IPs for an allowlist, then reset passwords and rotate API keys as KYT and Address Screening come back; Reactor and Data Solutions remain down while hardening continues. The Hacker News

entry.title: Internet & Cloud Health Digest — Nov 5, 2026
entry.summary: Beget (Russia); DigiCert; Zyxel GS1900 network switches; Apple devices (CVE-2024-27834 added to CISA’s exploited list); Linux servers running Control Web Panel (CWPdoor backdoor); SignalPlus; Queens Public Library (New York); Cloudflare had a network disruption across multiple India locations…
entry.content:
Daily internet & cloud health digest, Nov 5, 2026 (past 24 hours) Source: Scout run 2026-11-05-0600.md, with direct checks of Oracle Cloud, Azure, Cloudflare, GitHub, Elastic, OpenAI, Claude, EDI VAN status pages, CISA’s exploited-vulnerabilities list, and security news.

1. Cyber incidents

Beget (Russia)

  • Industry: Technology providers / web hosting, cloud and domain registrar
  • Threat actor: Unknown (no claim)
  • Date reported: Nov 3–4, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed (recovery under way)
  • Summary: Overnight Nov 1–2, attackers reached Beget’s infrastructure-management systems and ran wiper scripts that erased VPS, S3 and Kubernetes data plus all binary VPS backups; file-level backups survived. More than 1,000 servers must be checked by hand, and some sites are back while most shared hosting is expected to recover. Disruption hit businesses, government sites and Russia’s Chestny Znak product-labeling system.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High for anyone hosted there or depending on services that are, including retailers and manufacturers tied to Chestny Znak labeling; rotate any credentials stored on Beget servers.
  • Source: The Record, Kommersant

DigiCert

  • Industry: Technology providers / certificate authority
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 1–5, 2026 (full incident report Nov 1, wide coverage Nov 5)
  • Status: Confirmed
  • Summary: An internal archive of customer validation records was left reachable from the internet after a February 2025 migration, and a self-registered account without MFA read part of it from June 27 to July 2, 2026. Most of the data was business contact details, but a small minority of accounts included passports, driver’s licenses or utility bills. DigiCert says CA systems, CertCentral, DigiCert ONE, logins and certificates were not affected, and no certificates need replacing; it hasn’t said how many people were hit.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium. Exposed contact and ID data on certificate admins is useful for targeted phishing and impersonation against companies that buy certificates.
  • Source: Cybersecurity News, Zyphe summary of DigiCert’s report

Zyxel GS1900 network switches

  • Industry: Technology providers / network equipment
  • Threat actor: Kapibala
  • Date reported: Nov 4–5, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed (exploited Aug–Sep 2026; fixed firmware available)
  • Summary: Switch hacks once blamed on a June flaw actually used a separate zero-day, CVE-2026-107441, that bypassed the June patch and let attackers run commands as root; nearly 1,000 switches in 48 countries were compromised. Zyxel’s fix is firmware 2.90 Patch 3 (advisory Nov 3).
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium–high for small offices, plants and branch sites running GS1900 switches; patched-in-June devices were still vulnerable, so update and check for compromise.
  • Source: BleepingComputer, Zyxel advisory

Apple devices (CVE-2024-27834 added to CISA’s exploited list)

  • Industry: Technology providers
  • Threat actor: Unknown (info-stealer operators per CISA coverage)
  • Date reported: Nov 4, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed (patched in 2024)
  • Summary: CISA added an old, already-patched Apple WebKit flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after it was used to deliver info-stealing malware. Devices still running unpatched older Apple OS versions are the ones at risk.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low–medium; mainly a patch-hygiene check for older Macs and iPhones in the fleet.
  • Source: The Hacker News, CISA KEV

Linux servers running Control Web Panel (CWPdoor backdoor)

  • Industry: Technology providers / web hosting
  • Threat actor: Unknown (sample found alongside the Ebury backdoor)
  • Date reported: Nov 4–5, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed (real victims in the wild)
  • Summary: XLab found a trojanized build of cwpsrv, the web server behind the CWP admin panel, that sits dormant until it gets a signed, encrypted HTTP request, then runs attacker commands and hides the request from logs. It replaces versions 1.15.10 and 1.24.0 and had zero antivirus detections; more than 340,000 CWP panels are internet-facing.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium for hosting providers and businesses using CWP-managed servers; check for the ngx_http_integrity_helper socket and rotate panel credentials if infected.
  • Source: BleepingComputer, XLab

SignalPlus

  • Industry: Financial services / crypto trading tools
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 4–5, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed (services suspended)
  • Summary: SignalPlus says a compromised third-party Telegram account and a fake Teams invite led to an attack with under $82,000 in losses, which it will reimburse. Binance and Deribit revoked every SignalPlus-linked API key and say their own systems and funds weren’t affected.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium for traders who connected SignalPlus to other exchanges; revoke those keys.
  • Source: CoinDesk, PANews

Queens Public Library (New York)

  • Industry: Government / public library
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 5, 2026 (attack Nov 3)
  • Status: Investigating (services still down)
  • Summary: Ransomware knocked out the library’s website, app, public computers, Wi-Fi, self-checkout and digital media. All 66 branches stayed open, and the library is working with law enforcement on a recovery it says will take time.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low for businesses; possible patron-data exposure is not yet known.
  • Source: The Register, Gothamist

3. Internet, network, cloud and EDI VAN issues

  • Cloudflare had a network disruption across multiple India locations starting about 9:05 AM CST today and pulled nine PoPs from service, then cleared it. Status: resolved. Cloudflare Status
  • Cloudflare Durable Objects in Western Europe had increased errors from about 7:23 AM CST; a fix is in and it’s being monitored. Status: ongoing (monitoring). Cloudflare Status
  • Oracle Cloud shows Normal Performance and Azure has no active events. Cleo, SPS Commerce and TrueCommerce are operational, OpenText’s Middle East ME22 item is the same long-running one, and no new outage or security reports turned up for the other EDI VAN providers checked.

4. Status changes

  • Chainalysis breach went from confirmed, contact data only (Oct 31 digest) to confirmed exposure of names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all users, with some KYT accounts accessed; KYT, address screening and the login page were taken offline, and every user must reset passwords and rotate API keys. The Record, Chainalysis
  • DreamHost went from monitoring (Oct 27 digest) to a confirmed breach: its File Manager exposed FTP/SFTP logins for users who signed in from August through Oct 23, plus some webmail sessions and possibly mailbox contents. BleepingComputer, DreamHost
  • GitHub’s second major Actions incident from yesterday went from ongoing (monitoring) to resolved at 12:16 PM CST Nov 4. GitHub Status
  • Elastic Cloud’s mOLTP PrivateLink connectivity incident went from ongoing to resolved at 7:36 PM CST Nov 4. Elastic Status

entry.summary: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa (France); Managed service providers and their Microsoft 365 / Azure clients (Todyl “Key Eater” campaign); Organizations hit by APT29 watering-hole campaign (incl. U.S. chemical-industry site and Plerdy SEO script); Google Workspace users targeted by Calendar-invite session…
entry.content:
Daily internet & cloud health digest, Nov 4, 2026 (past 24 hours) Source: Scout run 2026-11-04-1200.md (also 2026-11-04-0600.md), with direct checks of Oracle Cloud, Azure, Cloudflare, GitHub, Elastic, OpenAI, Claude, EDI VAN status pages, CISA’s exploited-vulnerabilities list, and security news.

1. Cyber incidents

Crédit Mutuel Arkéa (France)

  • Industry: Financial services / banking
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 4, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed (contained; recovery under way)
  • Summary: The French regional bank confirmed a cyberattack that let attackers use the bank’s own account to send fraudulent transfers to other banks, then likely into crypto. Entry was through a supplier platform, not Fortuneo. Clients’ funds were not hit; some transfers were delayed while Arkéa paused activity. It did not confirm ZachXBT’s ~$133M / €118M figure but said losses are in that order of magnitude and not a threat to the bank’s soundness; some funds were blocked and recovery is ongoing.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High for banks and payment providers that trust supplier platforms for treasury or settlement access; a vendor compromise can move institutional funds without touching retail accounts.
  • Source: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa, AFP

Managed service providers and their Microsoft 365 / Azure clients (Todyl “Key Eater” campaign)

  • Industry: Technology providers / MSPs (downstream: government, energy, food & agriculture, transportation, education, legal, nonprofits)
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 3–4, 2026
  • Status: Ongoing
  • Summary: Todyl says that since Nov 1 one operator has been signing in as MSPs’ own Entra ID apps with stolen, still-valid secrets (and some Azure DevOps federated identities / session tokens), reaching about 45 app registrations across ~18 orgs and 27 organizations so far. App sign-ins skip MFA and user Conditional Access; the actor reads Key Vault, bulk-downloads credential and config files from SharePoint, and fans out through MSP multi-tenant / GDAP access. All confirmed activity came from 199.19.77.84; the latest attempt Todyl saw was blocked. No Microsoft vulnerability is involved.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Very high. One compromised MSP app can expose every client it manages; harvested secrets target VPNs, RMM, backups, firewalls, and AI keys.
  • Source: Todyl

Organizations hit by APT29 watering-hole campaign (incl. U.S. chemical-industry site and Plerdy SEO script)

  • Industry: Government / espionage targets (also commercial sites loading the compromised tracker)
  • Threat actor: APT29 (Midnight Blizzard), Russia-aligned per Sekoia
  • Date reported: Nov 4, 2026 (campaign window Aug 27–Sep 3 called out in coverage)
  • Status: Confirmed (patches available; campaign described as past window)
  • Summary: Sekoia attributes a watering-hole campaign that profiled visitors then delivered zero-click N-day exploit chains for already-patched iOS and Android/Chrome flaws, stealing cookies, messaging databases, Keychain data, location and photos. Compromised sites included a U.S. chemical industry trade association and a Ukrainian web-analytics script (Plerdy) loaded by thousands of sites. Apple and Google have patched the flaws used; updating devices is the fix. Malware does not survive a reboot.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium–high for anyone loading third-party analytics/SEO scripts, and for mobile fleets that lag on OS patches.
  • Source: Sekoia, BleepingComputer, The Hacker News

Google Workspace users targeted by Calendar-invite session phishing (“Operation CloudFire”)

  • Industry: Technology / enterprise productivity
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 4, 2026 (active since mid-August)
  • Status: Investigating (Material says the Google wave looks dispersed; dormant Microsoft 365 variant exists)
  • Summary: Material Security documented a campaign that sent Calendar invites from compromised, familiar senders, routed victims through Google’s own redirector to a reverse-proxied Google sign-in that relays MFA codes and number matching, capturing live sessions past MFA. Material took down 897 domains and blocked tens of thousands of messages; themes have shifted toward Drive share invites, and an unfinished Microsoft 365 branch was found but not activated.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium. Hijacked Workspace sessions reach mail, Drive, and OAuth grants in the victim’s name; review audit logs and revoke sessions quickly.
  • Source: BleepingComputer

NIKKE / Level Infinite (Tencent) PC launcher

  • Industry: Technology / gaming
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 4, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed (investigating impact)
  • Summary: Level Infinite confirmed that NIKKE PC launcher script files may have been tampered with; it patched the client around 11:30 AM CST Nov 3 and is assessing damage. Reporting says CDN JavaScript altered since late September put PC-launcher users at risk of a remote-access trojan that can steal browser passwords, tokens, API keys and crypto-wallet data. Mobile versions are not implicated; already-infected PCs need cleanup beyond the patch.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium for players and for any shared workstations that ran the launcher; rotate passwords, tokens, and wallet keys if the PC was used.
  • Source: Asiae / Level Infinite confirmation via Scout

Kyiv Independent

  • Industry: Media / news
  • Threat actor: Unknown (Russia suspected, not confirmed)
  • Date reported: Nov 4, 2026
  • Status: Investigating (unauthorized posts removed; donor/payment data reportedly not accessed)
  • Summary: Attackers gained access to the outlet’s CMS and a newsletter service on Nov 4 and sent false Russian- and English-language emails, including claims about a nuclear warhead aimed at Kyiv and fabricated Zelensky/Putin messaging. Staff deleted unauthorized site posts, told readers their banking/donor details appear untouched so far, and say the content points to a Russian operation.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low for most businesses; high reputational/info-ops impact for anyone amplifying unverified crisis emails.
  • Source: Kyiv Independent

3. Internet, network, cloud and EDI VAN issues

  • GitHub opened a second major Actions incident at 11:40 AM CST today (events that trigger Actions), mitigated with delayed job status updates still being monitored as of ~12:07 PM CST. Status: ongoing (monitoring). GitHub Status
  • GitHub Actions, Pages and Webhooks were degraded from about 10:05 to 11:01 AM CST and then resolved (separate from the early-morning outage below). Status: resolved. GitHub Status
  • Elastic Cloud still has a major mOLTP PrivateLink connectivity incident open since about 6:08 AM CST. Status: ongoing. Elastic Status
  • Cloudflare had Tokyo (NRT) network latency from about 7:39 to 9:33 AM CST. Status: resolved. Cloudflare Status
  • Oracle Cloud remains Normal Performance, Azure has no active events, and OpenAI and Claude report all systems operational. Cleo, SPS Commerce and TrueCommerce are operational with no new incidents. OpenText’s Middle East ME22 regional outage is still the same long-running investigating item, not a new event. No new outage or security reports turned up for the other EDI VAN providers checked.

4. Status changes

  • GitHub’s early-morning major incident (Pull Requests partial outage; Git Operations, Issues, and later Actions degraded) went from investigating/ongoing (alerted ~5:04 AM CST) to resolved at 5:50 AM CST. GitHub Status
  • WordPress core CVE-2026-119977 went from “exploit attempts seen” (Nov 1 digest) to confirmed active exploitation on CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (added Nov 3, due Nov 6; fix 7.1.4). CISA KEV
  • The European refrigeration / cold-chain cyberattacks expanded again: France’s blood service (EFS) confirmed cold-room monitoring at three sites was tampered with through its refrigeration contractor (setpoints raised; alarms caught it; no products lost; remote access cut). Still under investigation with Danfoss-linked controls previously confirmed elsewhere. Sud Ouest / Scout

entry.content:
Daily internet & cloud health digest, Nov 3, 2026 (past 24 hours) Source: Scout run 2026-11-03-0600.md, with direct checks of the Oracle Cloud, Azure, Cloudflare, AI provider and EDI VAN status pages, CISA's exploited-vulnerabilities list and security news.

1. Cyber incidents

WordPress sites running the CryptoPayment Gateway plugin

  • Industry: Retail / e-commerce (crypto payments)
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 3, 2026
  • Status: Investigating (exploitation attempts seen, no fix available)
  • Summary: Defused Cyber has seen attackers trying to exploit CVE-2026-81648 (CVSS 10) in the CryptoPayment Gateway plugin, versions 1.2.1 through 1.2.2, the latest release. The bug lets anyone with no login delete files on the server, rewrite the payment settings and pull stored wallet credentials in plain text, and WPScan lists no fix.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium for online stores taking crypto through this plugin; removing or disabling it is the only protection for now.
  • Source: The Hacker News

Enterprises with hijacked AI model accounts ("LLMjacking")

  • Industry: Financial services, Retail, Technology, Transportation
  • Threat actor: Unknown (multiple)
  • Date reported: Nov 2–3, 2026
  • Status: Ongoing
  • Summary: Google's Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant warned that attackers are stealing cloud AI API keys through phishing, leaked source code, misconfigured environments and exposed client-side code, then running up model usage on the victim's bill. Single incidents have cost some companies up to about $1 million in cloud charges, often within hours.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium. Any company with AI keys in code, CI pipelines or vendor apps should check for exposed keys and set spending alerts and caps.
  • Source: The Hacker News

Thousands of web apps built with Lovable

  • Industry: Technology providers (AI app builder)
  • Threat actor: None identified (researcher finding)
  • Date reported: Nov 3, 2026
  • Status: Ongoing
  • Summary: Security firm Crissy Field found that 24,664 of 34,545 Lovable-built apps using a Supabase database handed out database records with no sign-in, and records with email addresses on 7,403 sites. The worst cases exposed passport records, payment details, contracts, invoices and more than 200,000 chat messages; it's unknown whether anyone misused the data, and Lovable says customers are responsible for their own data handling.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium. Vendors or internal teams shipping quick AI-built apps may be leaking customer data without knowing it.
  • Source: India Today

Ukrainian law enforcement, justice, local government and defense organizations

  • Industry: Government
  • Threat actor: Gorbag (Russia-aligned, also tracked as UAC-0226)
  • Date reported: Nov 3, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed
  • Summary: ESET says Gorbag has been sending government-themed phishing emails, including ones exploiting a WinRAR flaw and macro-laden Excel files, to plant its BeautyStealer malware, which grabs browser data, VPN and RDP settings, password-manager databases and Office files. The group has hit only Ukrainian targets since early 2025.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low for U.S. businesses, though it's another reason to keep WinRAR patched.
  • Source: The Hacker News

3. Internet, network, cloud and EDI VAN issues

1. Cyber incidents

Delhaize, Carrefour, Spar, ICA and Coop supermarkets (Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden)

  • Industry: Retail / Food & Agriculture
  • Threat actor: Unknown (unclaimed)
  • Date reported: Nov 2, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: Overnight attacks switched off or overheated refrigerators and freezers at about 40 Delhaize and 15 Carrefour stores in Belgium, Spar shops in Belgium and Luxembourg, and several ICA and six Coop stores in Sweden, with some freezers set to 50°C and food lost. Delhaize's refrigeration contractor called it a cyberattack and Sweden's national cybersecurity center is investigating; it follows a similar attack on French supermarkets last month.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High. The way in appears to be a shared refrigeration-management contractor, so any grocer or cold-chain site using remotely managed refrigeration controls should check vendor remote access now.
  • Source: NBC News

Florida Department of Education (student financial aid website)

  • Industry: Government
  • Threat actor: Unknown (unclaimed)
  • Date reported: Nov 2, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed (contained)
  • Summary: Hackers breached FloridaStudentFinancialAidSG.org, discovered Oct 19, potentially exposing names, Social Security numbers, birth dates, addresses, phone numbers and emails of about 4.9 million people. The department says the breach is contained and limited to that site; how attackers got in hasn't been disclosed.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low for businesses directly, but the stolen SSNs raise identity-fraud and phishing risk for employees who applied for Florida aid.
  • Source: SecurityWeek

BTCPay Server (self-hosted Bitcoin payment processor)

  • Industry: Technology providers / fintech
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 1–2, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed (investigating)
  • Summary: Attackers drained Bitcoin and Litecoin hot wallets on merchant servers running BTCPay Server 2.4.1 or earlier, using a new way to exploit a flaw fixed in 2.4.2 and logging in with admin access. BTCPay says operators on old versions should sweep funds to a new wallet and rebuild on a fresh server, since updating alone won't remove attacker access; hosts like LunaNode took instances offline, and losses haven't been disclosed.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium for merchants accepting crypto through self-hosted BTCPay.
  • Source: BTCPay Server blog, Decrypt

Videostrong Android TV boxes (botnet takedown by Google)

  • Industry: Technology providers (consumer devices)
  • Threat actor: Device maker Videostrong (per Google) plus criminal buyers
  • Date reported: Nov 2, 2026
  • Status: Resolved (botnet disrupted; backdoor remains on devices)
  • Summary: Google took down the control servers of a 1.3-million-device botnet made up mostly of Android TV set-top boxes, saying it's highly confident Shenzhen maker Videostrong built in a backdoor called x.cpe and sold access for ad fraud and residential proxy traffic. The backdoor is still on the boxes and owners can't remove it.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium. Cheap Android TV boxes on home or office networks can relay attacker traffic, so they should be kept off business networks.
  • Source: The Hacker News

  • Industry: Multiple (enterprise)
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 2, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed
  • Summary: Microsoft investigated two intrusions where attackers posing as IT support on Teams talked employees into opening Quick Assist, then abused insecurely configured Active Directory Certificate Services to get certificates for privileged accounts, including a domain controller. In one case company data was copied out; no Teams flaw was used.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium. External-tenant Teams chats are a growing entry point, so restricting external Teams access and auditing AD CS templates is worthwhile.
  • Source: The Hacker News

  • Industry: Entertainment
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Nov 2, 2026

HYBE says the access routes are closed and it has seen no misuse, but hasn't said how many people were affected.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium. It's another breach that came in through a vendor's software.
  • Source: Korea JoongAng Daily

Ukraine's Air Alert app (and Russia's emergency alert app)

  • Industry: Government
  • Threat actor: Hitcore (claimed, unconfirmed by Ukraine)
  • Date reported: Nov 1–2, 2026
  • Status: Resolved
  • Summary: Ukraine's air-raid warning app pushed fake radiation, chemical and street-fighting alerts for about an hour before they were cleared; a Russian group called Hitcore says it phished an administrator. Hours later Russia's Emergencies Ministry said its own alert app was hit by a cyberattack that sent fake information.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low outside the region.

Israeli target and Kurdistan Region of Iraq government cloud

  • Industry: Government
  • Threat actor: DarkBlinders (Iran-nexus)
  • Date reported: Nov 2, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed
  • Summary: Dream Research Labs says DarkBlinders ran spear-phishing with trojanized utilities from August to October, compromising a high-profile individual in Israel and a government cloud environment in Iraq's Kurdistan Region.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low for U.S. businesses.
  • Source: The Hacker News

  • Industry: Technology providers / crypto

  • Summary: Attackers got into the publishing portal and listed a fake "SKR Claim" airdrop app that asked for seed phrases for about an hour before Solana Mobile pulled it, wiped it from devices and fixed the bug.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low.

  • Industry: Technology providers / Government
  • Threat actor: Unknown (suspected China-nexus, AI-assisted)

  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High. SD-WAN controllers sit at the center of company and supplier networks, so anyone still unpatched should update, hunt for compromise and consider rotating keys.

  • Industry: Technology providers
  • Threat actor: Unknown (Pluto Security assesses a financially motivated, Chinese-speaking operator)
  • Date reported: Oct 29, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed (ongoing)

The campaign came back within days of a takedown, and a near-identical copy was still live when BleepingComputer reported it.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium to high for teams running self-hosted AI inference or CI jobs that pull models, since infected machines should be treated as compromised.

Daily internet & cloud health digest, Oct 29, 2026 (past 24 hours) Source: Scout run 2026-10-29-0600.md (plus Scout's 2026-10-28-1800.md and 2026-10-29-0000.md runs for the rest of the window), with direct checks of the cloud, EDI VAN and Cloudflare status pages, CISA's exploited-vulnerability list and BleepingComputer.

1. Cyber incidents

U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS, CBP, ICE)

  • Industry: Government
  • Threat actor: Hacktivists ("Icepick" leak, published by Distributed Denial of Secrets)
  • Date reported: Oct 28, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: Distributed Denial of Secrets published names, phone numbers and assignments of about 40,000 DHS, CBP and ICE employees, reportedly pulled from a DHS Okta single sign-on directory. WIRED verified parts of the data, and Okta denies its own systems were compromised.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium. If the data came from a misconfigured or abused identity directory, other agencies and contractors using the same setup could be exposed, and the leaked staff details invite targeted phishing.
  • Source: X news summary

Unnamed California city (police and 911 data)

  • Industry: Government
  • Threat actor: Rhysida
  • Date reported: Oct 28, 2026
  • Status: Claimed
  • Summary: Rhysida posted a leak-site listing claiming police and 911 data from a California city it didn't name. The claim hasn't been verified.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low for business, but it's a public-safety system.
  • Source: RansomNews

EWM Group (Peacocks, Bonmarché)

  • Industry: Retail
  • Threat actor: Aurora
  • Date reported: Oct 28, 2026
  • Status: Claimed
  • Summary: The Aurora group listed the UK fashion retailer EWM Group, which owns Peacocks and Bonmarché, on its leak site. Neither the scope nor the claim has been confirmed.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium for its suppliers and logistics partners if order or partner data was taken.
  • Source: RansomNews

Chrome Web Store search-hijacking campaign

  • Industry: Technology providers
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 29, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed
  • Summary: Researchers found 319 Chrome extensions, with about 13.4 million combined installs, quietly sending users' searches through tracking servers to make advertising money from Bing and Yahoo.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium. Unvetted browser extensions on work PCs can see and redirect browsing traffic, so it's worth auditing what's installed.
  • Source: BleepingComputer

Ledger hardware wallets sold in Singapore

  • Industry: Technology / retail (hardware supply chain)
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 29, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: Singapore police say tampered Ledger hardware wallets sold through local retailers stole recovery phrases, costing two users about $2.7 million. Ledger has asked resellers in the region to stop sales while it reviews.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High for hardware bought through third-party resellers, since the devices were compromised before they reached buyers.
  • Source: X news summary

Morrison Foerster

  • Industry: Legal services
  • Threat actor: SilentRansomGroup
  • Date reported: Oct 28, 2026
  • Status: Claimed
  • Summary: SilentRansomGroup listed the US law firm Morrison Foerster on its leak site. The firm hasn't confirmed an incident.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium, because large law firms hold confidential deal and litigation files for many corporate clients.
  • Source: RansomNews

zkLink Nova bridge

  • Industry: Crypto / fintech
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 29, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: An attacker drained about $786,000 from the zkLink Nova Ethereum bridge late Oct 28 by reusing a valid message hash to forge withdrawals. zkLink paused the affected contracts and offered a 20% bounty.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low outside crypto.
  • Source: X news summary

Virtualine bulletproof hosting (law enforcement action)

  • Industry: Cybercrime infrastructure
  • Threat actor: Virtualine (hosting used by ransomware and other criminals)
  • Date reported: Oct 28, 2026
  • Status: Resolved (domain seized)
  • Summary: U.S. law enforcement seized the main domain of Virtualine, a hosting service advertised on crime forums for ransomware and other illegal activity.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Positive in the short term, though such groups usually move to new hosting quickly.
  • Source: BleepingComputer

2. AI service outages

  • Grok Bot, Cloud Agents and Origin were degraded from about 4:15 PM CDT Oct 28 for roughly two hours, leaving many bots unresponsive before service recovered. Status: resolved. X news summary

3. Internet, network, cloud and EDI VAN issues

  • A deep-sea fiber cut near Mtunzini, South Africa damaged the Seacom and EASSy submarine cables, slowing Safaricom home fiber and other Kenyan internet providers while traffic shifts to backup cables. Status: ongoing (repairs expected to take about a week). X news summary
  • Bet365 customers in several countries couldn't log in or saw missing bets for about two hours during Oct 28 evening football matches. Status: resolved. X news summary
  • AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure (no active events) and Oracle Cloud (Normal Performance) had no new incidents, and Cloudflare had only a few short, minor incidents that are all resolved. The EDI VAN pages I could read show nothing new: Cleo, SPS Commerce and TrueCommerce are all operational, and OpenText lists only an old Middle East item from May. I couldn't read the DiCentral, Descartes or ECGrid pages.

4. Status changes

entry.content:
Daily internet & cloud health digest, Oct 28, 2026 (past 24 hours) Sources: Scout run 2026-10-28-1200.md (plus Scout's 1800, 0000 and 0600 runs) and direct checks of the EDI VAN, AI and CDN status pages.

1. Cyber incidents

Federal Election Commission (FEC)

  • Industry: Government
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 27, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: The FEC took its web-facing services offline, including electronic filing, after a "bad actor" tried to breach its systems around 9 PM CDT on Oct 26. The system was still offline Wednesday morning. Nobody has confirmed a successful intrusion or data theft, and voting isn't affected.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low for business, but campaign-finance filers can't submit their 24- and 48-hour reports a week before the midterms.
  • Sources: Politico, CNBC

Volt Typhoon "Silent Train" framework

  • Industry: Technology providers and critical infrastructure (network devices)
  • Threat actor: Volt Typhoon (China)
  • Date reported: Oct 28, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: Researchers found Volt Typhoon chaining hijacked routers, IoT devices and business network gear into short-lived relay paths. The paths are rebuilt daily and hide zero-day attacks. The exploited flaws include CVE-2026-16812, CVE-2026-20127 and a suspected zero-day in Quest KACE.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High, because edge and network devices at any company can be quietly used as relays for attacks.
  • Sources: BleepingComputer, CyberScoop

GitHub "Gheist" token-theft campaign / Dodo Payments

  • Industry: Technology providers
  • Threat actor: Unknown ("Gheist" campaign)
  • Date reported: Oct 27–28, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: Someone deleted a private Dodo Payments repository through the GitHub command-line tool, and the deletion left no trace in the audit log. Researchers tie it to a campaign using stolen tokens that has hit more than 850 GitHub accounts. GitHub is investigating.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High for software supply chains, since stolen developer tokens can be used to change or delete code.
  • Source: X news summary

Oracle E-Business Suite CVE-2026-101767

  • Industry: Technology providers (an ERP system widely used in manufacturing and logistics)
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 27, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: Attackers have started probing a critical flaw that Oracle patched on Oct 20. It lets an attacker who isn't logged in use SQL injection to run code on the server. Defused's decoy systems have caught attempts, but there are no confirmed compromises yet, and CISA hasn't added it to its list of exploited vulnerabilities.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High if attackers get it working, because EBS runs orders, finance and supply-chain work at many large companies. Patch now.
  • Sources: BleepingComputer, SecurityWeek

Convertr (Brazilian e-commerce platform)

  • Industry: Retail
  • Threat actor: A Magecart card-skimming group focused on Brazil
  • Date reported: Oct 26–27, 2026
  • Status: Resolved (skimmer removed, but how much damage it did is disputed)
  • Summary: Attackers planted a card skimmer in the Plausible analytics script that Convertr hosts itself and loads on every Convertr checkout. From Oct 24 to 27 it stole card details and taxpayer IDs. Convertr has removed it and says no real store checkouts were affected, but Sansec's findings dispute that.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High. It's a textbook case of one shared third-party script hitting dozens of merchant checkouts at once.
  • Sources: BleepingComputer, Sansec

Sony Network Communications (So-net / plala)

  • Industry: Telecom / ISP
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 27, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed
  • Summary: An Oct 19 intrusion at the Japanese internet providers So-net and plala exposed personal details of about 2.59 million current and former customers, along with about 54,000 email passwords. Sony shut the servers down on Oct 23 and has reset the affected passwords.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low outside Japan's consumer customers, apart from the phishing risk.
  • Sources: So-net notice, Help Net Security

Coinbase / Amplitude

  • Industry: Financial services (through a third-party analytics vendor)
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 27–28, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed
  • Summary: Coinbase told some customers that a security incident at its analytics vendor Amplitude exposed their contact details. Coinbase says its own systems and customer funds weren't affected.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium, because Amplitude serves many companies and their customers may be exposed too.
  • Source: X news summary

Bithumb and Daishin Securities (South Korea)

  • Industry: Financial services
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 27–28, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: The crypto exchange Bithumb found hackers in its internal groupware on Oct 27. Separately, Daishin Securities said data on 38,490 customers was exposed. Regulators are opening inspections.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low for US supply chains.
  • Source: X news summary

Solflare

  • Industry: Crypto / fintech
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 28, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed
  • Summary: A breach at Solflare's staking provider exposed validator keys and paused rewards on about 1.56 million SOL. Solflare says no user funds were lost and is moving stakers to a new validator.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low. The breach came in through Solflare's staking provider.
  • Source: X news summary

2. AI service outages

  • Some GitHub Copilot models from OpenAI and Microsoft were partly unavailable from 9:12 to 10:28 AM CDT today because of a problem at an upstream provider. Status: resolved. GitHub Status

3. Internet, network, cloud and EDI VAN issues

  • YouTube had widespread playback errors in the US and elsewhere, with Downdetector reports peaking near 24,000. Most of it cleared within about two hours. Status: resolved. X news summary
  • Sign-in to Revolut's app was partly down for about 44 minutes in the UK and Europe today. Status: resolved. RTÉ
  • Safaricom's M-Pesa mobile-money service went down across Kenya early Oct 28. It doesn't affect US users. Status: ongoing as of Scout's 6 AM CDT run. X news summary
  • Cloudflare has had minor network performance issues at its Ashburn, Virginia location since about 11:39 PM CDT last night. Status: ongoing (monitoring). Cloudflare Status
  • AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and Oracle Cloud had no new incidents. The EDI VAN status pages I checked show nothing new: SPS Commerce, TrueCommerce/DiCentral, Cleo and OpenText. I couldn't read Descartes' status page.

4. Status changes

  • Tailscale "Tailworm" flaws went from patches promised to fixed in Tailscale v1.104.4, under security bulletins TS-2026-014 through TS-2026-017. Update your clients, especially if you use Tailscale SSH. Tailscale
  • UNM Health went from investigating to critical systems restored and hospitals reopened. The Byod ransomware group claims it hit 36,000 systems and stole data, which UNM hasn't confirmed. UNM HSC, nm.news
  • The GMO Onamae.com Desktop Cloud breach went from ongoing to stolen customer and company data being published after GMO refused to pay the ransom. TechCrunch
